chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, regarding

a man who died and bequeathed that Hajj be performed for him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was the first Hajj, Hajj is performed for him from the middle of the wealth, and if it was other than the first Hajj, then it is from the one-third.'

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The one-third portion of the estate designated for bequests and specific obligations
key_terms.صَرُورَةً: The first obligatory Hajj performed in one's lifetime or bequeathed as the primary duty
key_terms.وَسَطِ الْمَالِ: The middle of the wealth, implying the entire estate or the main portion before deducting debts/heirs' shares in this context

ai.seo_question: How is the cost of Hajj for a deceased person calculated from their estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the financial priority of Hajj in an estate, distinguishing between the first obligatory Hajj (al-sarurah), which is deducted from the principal wealth before bequests, and subsequent Hajjs, which are paid from the one-third share reserved for wills. This ruling ensures that the primary religious duty is fulfilled with the highest priority, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the completeness of the deceased's spiritual obligations before distributing residual assets.
